kicker: Hy4 flash and its Engram tables

scenes.headline: How Hy4 flash looks parameters up instead of multiplying them
scenes.sub: Four hashed n-gram tables beside a mixture-of-experts
scenes.say: I'm Modulus. Tencent's Hy4 flash stores two hundred and twenty billion parameters, and a quarter of them are never multiplied by anything. They are looked up.

states.say: Sixty-three billion of them sit in four Engram tables, outside the experts. A token reads sixty-four rows of those tables, about twelve kilobytes.
Everything a token actually computes with comes to about eleven billion. So the big number is a storage number, not a compute number.

params.table: one table per Engram layer, 31.68 GB
params.home: the table stays in host memory

steps.say: Take the word Great, after Alexander the. Each token id is first swapped for a canonical id.
steps.term: Canonical id: one id for every spelling

steps.say: The, capital The, all-caps THE, even the Vietnamese word with accents, all fold into one id. The vocabulary shrinks by about a quarter.
Each id is multiplied by its own odd constant. XOR the last two and you have the bigram key. XOR in the third and you have the trigram key.
Eight heads take the bigram key modulo eight different primes, and eight more do the same with the trigram key. Each remainder is a row.
steps.term: Hash head: one prime, one row

steps.say: Those sixteen rows are all this layer reads. Nothing in the address depends on the hidden state, so it is known before the layer runs.
The design is DeepSeek's Engram. The rows from every head are joined, and the hidden state gates them before they reach the residual stream.
steps.caption: DeepSeek's Engram module

steps.say: Hy4 flash keeps the hashing and the gate. Like DeepSeek's own release, it drops the convolution at the end, and it adds a twist to the gate.
Because the address needs only token ids, I computed all sixty-four of them on a laptop.
Each table sits alone in a shard, so a row is at a fixed byte offset in Tencent's own files.
Sixty-four range requests brought back twelve thousand two hundred and eighty-eight bytes. Lower-case great lands on the same rows.

parts.note: gate: a square-root sigmoid of key times hidden state
parts.say: Each of the four residual streams computes a gate from its own hidden state and the memory's key.

parts.note: a learned offset no gate multiplies
parts.say: Then comes something the paper does not have: a learned offset per stream, added to the gate.

parts.note: one value, shared by all four streams
parts.say: The sum scales one shared value vector. If the offset is large, the gate can no longer switch the memory off.

scenes.title: First Engram layer against the last

left.title: Layer 1
items: The gate decides: off or on
left.say: At the first Engram layer the offsets are tiny, so the gate works as the paper intends, a switch.

right.title: Layer 31
right.say: At the last one, stream zero's offset is about minus one point one. Its multiplier never reaches zero, so the memory always arrives.

scenes.title: Wikitext-2 perplexity against normal
scenes.note: Q3_K GGUF on a CPU, 20,480 tokens
scenes.say: I tested that on a CPU. With the tables off, perplexity rises seventeen percent. With the rows scrambled, it nearly doubles. Wrong memory hurts more than none, because the gate cannot shut it out.

steps.say: How much to spend on memory? The paper found loss is lowest with three quarters to four fifths of the idle budget in experts.
Hy4 flash puts sixty-nine point four percent there, a little further toward memory, on a curve measured at a much smaller scale.
steps.caption: Hy4 flash: 69.4% in experts

scenes.title: Engram tables, share of the download
scenes.note: quantizing the experts leaves the tables
scenes.say: Quantize the rest of the model and the tables become a bigger share of what you download. The FP8 release keeps them in sixteen-bit.

items.say: The transformers port keeps the tables off the accelerator.
The llama dot cpp port hashes every layer first and prefetches the rows.
And on a Mac with a hundred and twenty-eight gigabytes, the table stays on the SSD while the model runs.

scenes.text: Eleven billion parameters do the math; sixty-three billion only need an address and somewhere cheap to live.
scenes.say: Eleven billion parameters do the math. Sixty-three billion only need an address, and somewhere cheap to live.

recap: Hash the last tokens into sixteen rows
A gate with an offset it cannot cancel
Tables in host memory, backbone on the GPU
scenes.say: Hash the tokens, gate the rows, and keep the tables on the host.
